subject: chemistry
title: IR Infrared: Bonds That Vibrate
welcome_lead: Identify functional groups from characteristic IR absorptions.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on IR spectroscopy interpretation.
final_note: You can hear the vibrations of bonds in cm^-1.

concepts.def: Absorbs IR to excite bond vibrations.

walkthroughs.body_html:
C-H ~3000 cm^-1. C=O 1680-1750. O-H alcohol 3230-3550 (broad). O-H carboxylic 2500-3300 (very broad).

N-H 3300-3500 (narrow). C-O ester 1000-1300. C=C 1620-1680 (weak/medium).

Broad O-H above 3200 + strong C=O near 1700 = carboxylic acid.

Broad O-H above 3200, no C=O = alcohol. Strong C=O alone = ketone or aldehyde (use NMR/Tollens' to distinguish).

Below 1500 cm^-1 contains overlapping bands unique to each compound.

Match unknown to a database spectrum to identify exact compound. Useful for distinguishing isomers (e.g. propan-1-ol vs propan-2-ol).

mcqs.q: What is the role of the fingerprint region (below ~1500 cm^-1) in IR spectroscopy?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
The fingerprint region is used to identify which functional groups are present.
The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
It is unique to each compound — used to identify a specific molecule by matching to a known spectrum.

mcqs.q: What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.

mcqs.q: In 1H NMR, what does the n+1 rule predict?
options: The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
Splitting tells you how many protons are in the same chemical environment as the one giving the peak.
A proton with n equivalent neighbouring protons will appear as a peak split into n+1 sub-peaks.
The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
